intervals.label: R&D project and proposed NaI cryogenic calorimeter at LNGS
intervals.note: Year of the first COSINUS paper read (March 2016), which describes the R&D project and the planned proof-of-principle detector, tested in dilution refrigerators at LNGS; 'The construction of the experimental facility is foreseen to start by 2021 at the INFN Gran Sasso National Laboratory (LNGS)' (arXiv:2106.07390). No approval date is published in the sources read.
intervals.quote: Both refrigerators are located in the LNGS underground site for obvious reasons of shielding against cosmic radiation.

intervals.label: construction of the experimental facility at LNGS
intervals.note: 'The step-by-step installation and commissioning of the main components of the experimental facility at LNGS (water tank, cleanroom, control building, electrical infrastructure) began in 2021 and was completed in 2023'; the dilution refrigerator was installed from spring 2024 (arXiv:2507.02429).
intervals.quote: COSINUS was constructed from 2021 to 2024 in the Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS) underground laboratories in central Italy.

intervals.label: underground run of a 3.67 g NaI remoTES prototype at LNGS
intervals.note: Prototype detector in a dilution refrigerator at LNGS (hall not named), separate from the COSINUS-1pi cryostat; its data gave the first underground COSINUS limit (11.6 g d, 76 h of background data).
intervals.quote: In total about ten days of stream data were taken over the first two weeks of June, 2022.

intervals.label: commissioning of the cryostat and facility; first physics run (COSINUS-1pi Run1) awaited
intervals.note: The cryostat was first cooled to 9.3 mK in spring 2024 and the experiment was inaugurated on 18 April 2024 (MPP news). Run 1 with eight NaI modules was planned for 'late 2025' (arXiv:2507.02429) and then 'mid 2026' (undated Heidelberg seminar abstract, probably 2026); the July 2026 review still says 'The experiment is currently being commissioned at the LNGS' (arXiv:2607.24448, Sec. 4.2). No source read reports physics data taking.
intervals.quote: In a second commissioning run in July 2024, the system was equipped with internal passive shielding: a 190 kg block of ultra-pure copper mounted on the Still plate at approximately 800 mK.

module_count.quote: Data taking with eight NaI detector modules (COSINUS1$\pi$ Run1) is planned to begin in late 2025.

tank_height.quote: A 7m tall, 7m wide instrumented water tank, designed to moderate the extenal neutron flux.

temperature.quote: During the first cooldown, the cryostat successfully reached a base temperature of 9.3 mK and demonstrated the required cooling power.

summary.plain: COSINUS is a dark matter detector being commissioned at the Gran Sasso laboratory in Italy. It uses sodium iodide crystals, the DAMA/LIBRA material, cooled to a few thousandths of a degree above absolute zero so that it senses both heat and light, to test whether DAMA's yearly signal is dark matter.
summary.technical: Undoped NaI crystals operated as cryogenic scintillating calorimeters: phonon channel read by transition edge sensors on a carrier crystal (remoTES) and light channel by a silicon beaker detector, giving event-by-event e/gamma versus nuclear-recoil discrimination and a low nuclear-recoil threshold; dry dilution refrigerator (9.3 mK reached) in a 7 m water tank with a Cherenkov muon veto of about 30 PMTs, in Hall B of LNGS (3600 m.w.e.). COSINUS-1pi Run 1: eight modules, goal 100 kg d; Run 2: up to 1000 kg d. Prototype: 441 eV nuclear-recoil baseline resolution (3.67 g crystal); O(pb) spin-independent sensitivity with 11.6 g d (underground, 2023).

technology.quote: The detectors must be cooled to milli-Kelvin temperatures in order to operate as bolometers.
technology.value: Undoped NaI crystals operated as cryogenic scintillating calorimeters (phonon and light read-out) in a dry dilution refrigerator inside a water-tank shield and muon veto
